headline: 6 newborns dead: Ad-din Hospital executive director resigns
summary: Dr Sheikh Mohiuddin stepped down following the deaths of six infants. The hospital is now implementing infrastructure changes and new supervisory protocols.
details: Dr Sheikh Mohiuddin has voluntarily resigned as the executive director of Ad-din Medical College Hospital after the deaths of six newborns.
Prof Jamalun Nessa, a former Dhaka University microbiology professor with a PhD from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, has been appointed to replace him.
The Ad-din Foundation stated that action has already been taken against staff members on charges of negligence of duty based on a preliminary investigation.
The foundation is now working to strengthen its supervisory system and re-evaluate patient care protocols to prevent future tragedies.
Infrastructure developments are underway to improve air circulation, light, and oxygen availability within the facility.
As part of these changes, the hospital has completely closed a bakery that was located above the corporate office.
The Ad-din Foundation operates nine hospitals and five medical colleges, providing healthcare to millions of underprivileged people since 1980.
caption:
Six newborns dead. The executive director of Ad-din Medical College Hospital has resigned.

Dr Sheikh Mohiuddin has voluntarily resigned as the executive director of Ad-din Medical College Hospital after the deaths of six newborns.

Prof Jamalun Nessa, a former Dhaka University microbiology professor with a PhD from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, has been appointed to replace him.

The Ad-din Foundation stated that action has already been taken against staff members on charges of negligence of duty based on a preliminary investigation.

The foundation is now working to strengthen its supervisory system and re-evaluate patient care protocols to prevent future tragedies.

Infrastructure developments are underway to improve air circulation, light, and oxygen availability within the facility.

As part of these changes, the hospital has completely closed a bakery that was located above the corporate office.

The Ad-din Foundation operates nine hospitals and five medical colleges, providing healthcare to millions of underprivileged people since 1980.

headline_marked: Footballer [[Jamal Bhuyan makes acting debut]] in new series
headline: Footballer Jamal Bhuyan makes acting debut in new series
summary: The Bangladesh national team captain takes the lead role in 'Brazentina', an eight-episode series inspired by the FIFA World Cup.
details: Bangladesh national football team captain Jamal Bhuyan is stepping in front of the camera for the first time as an actor, playing the central character in an eight-episode series titled 'Brazentina'.
The series, directed by Tarique Muhammad Hasan, is inspired by the passion surrounding the FIFA World Cup and will premiere on the OTT platform iScreen on June 30.
Filming took place at a football ground in Kalabagan, Dhaka, a location that holds special significance for Jamal as it is where he started his football career.
Jamal revealed that he initially turned down the offer, but was eventually convinced by the director and encouragement from former cricketer Mohammad Ashraful.
While Jamal has appeared in advertisements, he admitted that acting is a new and challenging experience, describing the process as 'magical' and working alongside professional performers.
Director Tarique Muhammad Hasan praised the footballer's commitment and sincerity, noting that he adapted remarkably well to the acting language in a short time.
The series also stars professional actors Tasnuva Tisha, Lamima Lam, Sharaf Ahmed Zibon, Shahid Un Nabi, and Ishtiaq Ahmed.
caption:
From the pitch to the screen! ⚽️🎬

National team captain Jamal Bhuyan is trading his boots for a lead acting role.

Bangladesh national football team captain Jamal Bhuyan is stepping in front of the camera for the first time as an actor, playing the central character in an eight-episode series titled 'Brazentina'.

The series, directed by Tarique Muhammad Hasan, is inspired by the passion surrounding the FIFA World Cup and will premiere on the OTT platform iScreen on June 30.

Filming took place at a football ground in Kalabagan, Dhaka, a location that holds special significance for Jamal as it is where he started his football career.

Jamal revealed that he initially turned down the offer, but was eventually convinced by the director and encouragement from former cricketer Mohammad Ashraful.

While Jamal has appeared in advertisements, he admitted that acting is a new and challenging experience, describing the process as 'magical' and working alongside professional performers.

Director Tarique Muhammad Hasan praised the footballer's commitment and sincerity, noting that he adapted remarkably well to the acting language in a short time.

The series also stars professional actors Tasnuva Tisha, Lamima Lam, Sharaf Ahmed Zibon, Shahid Un Nabi, and Ishtiaq Ahmed.
